title: Zero-friction stub + metering — developer onramp voice & pricing experiments
content:
Purpose:
This brief proposes a low‑friction developer onramp for Redwood Hosted API that prioritizes immediate feedback, transparent metering, and minimal commitment. The aim is to reduce time-to-first-use, increase trial-to-paid conversions, and surface pricing clarity before surprises hit invoices.

High-level hypothesis:
If we give engineers an instant stub endpoint + visible per-request metering and a tiny commitment option, they’ll: 1) test faster, 2) build real integrations sooner, and 3) be more likely to convert because they understand unit economics.

Core developer-first value props to emphasize (voice guidance):
- Instant sandbox: "Start sending requests in seconds — no credit card required."
- Predictable economics: "Clear per-token and per-embed meters so engineers can model costs before committing."
- Non-blocking experiment flow: "Try a short-lived dedicated slot or burstable tokens if you need predictable latency — switch later without rework."
- Production continuity: "Same API, same auth, same SDKs from prototype to production (no re-architecting)."
- Low cognitive load: concise examples, 3-line quickstarts, and one-click sample projects.

Target quickstart flows (3 variants — prioritized):
1) Quick Try (zero friction)
   - Steps: (a) Open Playground, (b) paste sample JSON, (c) hit "Run" — returns streaming output and a small estimated cost badge.
   - Outcome: time-to-first-response < 30s, no billing required, ephemeral API key with 100 free tokens.
2) Lightweight Experiment (credit card optional)
   - Steps: Create a scoped API key, send up to 1M free trial tokens for 14 days, view live meter in console.
   - Outcome: team can prototype an integration and estimate monthly cost at current usage pattern.
3) Commitment Lite (paid, small monthly)
   - Steps: Choose "Commitment Lite" (monthly $99 usable as credits) to unlock longer-lived keys, reserved latency band, and 50% off quantized model tiers for test runs.
   - Outcome: removes rate limits, small financial commitment that signals intent and boosts conversion probability.

Pricing language drafts (customer-facing microcopy):
- Playground tier: "Sandbox mode — 100 free tokens, ephemeral key. Ideal for immediate exploration."
- Pay-as-you-go: "Metered per token/embedding. No minimums, pause anytime."
- Commitment Lite: "Small monthly credit to remove sandbox limits and access reserved capacity. Billed monthly, usable across teams."
- Cost estimator pitch: "Estimate your cost in the Console — plug in expected calls per minute and average tokens to see monthly spend and latency tier tradeoffs."

Billing UI copy snippets (for console and checkout):
- CTA: "Estimate cost" -> opens quick calculator modal with sample routes and typical token counts.
- Badge: "Estimated run cost: $0.003 — view detailed breakdown" (click expands token vs compute vs quantization cost)
- Tooltip: "Commitment Lite gives you reserved throughput and a predictable bill; unused credits roll over for 2 billing cycles."

Competitive notes (short analysis focused on GTM positioning):
- OpenAI: excellent dev ergonomics and brand recognition; weakness = opaque compute vs model pricing and less fine-grained reserved latency controls. Positioning: "More transparent unit economics and smoother path to dedicated/reserved capacity for teams growing from prototype to production."
- Anthropic: safety/guardrails focus; less emphasis on production economics. Positioning: "We match safety features where needed but keep pricing and performance visible to engineers."
- Cloud providers (AWS/Azure/GCP): integrated infra but higher ops burden and inconsistent SDK UX. Positioning: "Lower ops/time-to-value vs building your own endpoints and a unified runtime for switching hardware or regions."

Common objections + proposed micro-responses:
- "How much will this cost at scale?" -> "Use our console estimator and sample templates; most teams get an accurate mid-month projection after 2–3 days of traffic because we provide per-route token breakouts and model-level compute multipliers."
- "I can use OpenAI for prototypes." -> "True — but Redwood gives you clearer unit economics and a migration path to dedicated/reserved capacity without changing your API or client code."
- "What if we need on-prem?" -> "Same API surface — Redwood Private supports VPC or on-prem with the same billing model for consistency."

A/B experiment ideas (to run against homepage/console flows):
- Variant A: "Zero-friction" hero CTA (Playground) + sample response pricing badge.
- Variant B: "Start a 14-day prototype" (more explicit trial) + brief cost estimator inline.
- Measure: click-to-first-call, time-to-first-call, trial-to-paid within 30/60/90 days, and average first-month spend.

KPIs to track for this experiment:
- Activation: percent of visitors who make first API call within 5 minutes.
- Engagement: number of distinct keys created per account during trial.
- Conversion: percent converting to any paid tier within 90 days.
- Cost awareness: percent of trial users who view the cost estimator before first paid action.
- Churn: percentage who cancel Commitment Lite within first 2 months.

Voice & tone guidelines for microcopy:
- Keep it engineer-forward: concise, technical, and example-first. Use exact numbers when possible (e.g., token counts, millis latency) — engineers model with numbers.
- Be transparent: if an estimate is rough, say so and show assumptions used.
- Empathize with billing anxiety: use reassuring language like "estimate", "projection", "sample run", and "reserved option" rather than ambiguous terms like "premium".

Sample landing hero lines (variants):
- "From prototype to production — same API, predictable costs." (concise, steady tone)
- "Start with a zero‑friction sandbox. Metered visibility, upgrade on your terms." (emphasizes method)
- "Build fast, measure cost, scale predictably." (action oriented)

Next steps (near-term plan):
1) Implement Playground ephemeral keys + 100 free tokens (engineering backlog ticket: GT-3421).
2) Wire cost estimator modal in Console (design + frontend).
3) Create Commitment Lite product spec and pricing guardrails (legal + finance review).
4) Run homepage A/B variants for 6 weeks, analyze cohorts, iterate on messaging.

Open questions and risks to validate:
- Does 100 free tokens provide enough signal for meaningful prototype? Might need to increase to 1k for certain embeddings/text tasks.
- Does Commitment Lite cannibalize larger reserved capacity sales if priced incorrectly? Need finance sensitivity analysis.
- Operational risk: ephemeral keys abuse — plan to rate limit and monitor automated scraping.

Appendix: Suggested quick code snippets (Console + README) — keep to a single 3-line example in each place, e.g.:
1) curl example for hero: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <EPHEMERAL_KEY>' -d '{"prompt":"Hello","max_tokens":16}'
2) JS example for Quickstart cards: const res = await client.generate({model:"rw-small",prompt:"Summarize...",max_tokens:32});

End — feedback requested from engineering (Ethan), product (Priya), and finance (Liam) on feasibility and cost guardrails.
